methodological_rigor.justification: The study employs a comprehensive multi-platform approach combining conditional knockout mice (STING and TOX cKO/cKD), adoptive cell transfer (ACT) models, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex immunofluorescence, and human tumor specimens (n=123 IHC cohort). Multiple orthogonal assays (ferroptosis inhibitors, iron chelation, gene knockdown/overexpression) validate the proposed mechanistic axis. Sample sizes in in vitro experiments are modest (n=3 biologically independent experiments, 3-5 mice/group), which is standard for mechanistic preclinical work. Statistical methods (one-way ANOVA, unpaired t-test, Wilcoxon, log-rank) are appropriate for the respective data types. Minor concern: the HO-1 paradox (suppressor vs. driver of ferroptosis) is acknowledged but the mechanistic reconciliation through iron-overloaded mitochondria is partially data-supported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is primarily a preclinical mechanistic study in murine tumor models and cell lines, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. The human translational component (n=123 cervical cancer IHC cohort and scRNA-seq from 2 patients) provides meaningful clinical associations between TOX/HO-1 expression and survival outcomes. However, direct clinical applicability of targeting the STING-TOX-HO-1 axis in engineered T-cell therapy requires validation in human settings; the engineering approach (genetic KO of STING/TOX) faces significant practical barriers for clinical translation. The mechanistic insight into ferroptosis resistance has potential relevance for improving ACT and ICB strategies.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports mouse studies with clear compliance with animal ethics (IRB approval, pathogen-free conditions, tumor volume limits) and provides a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary. Bulk RNA-seq data is deposited in GSA (CRA011572) and human scRNA-seq in GSA-Human (HRA003358), enabling data access. Reagent details are provided in Supplementary Dataset 1. Group sizes are consistently reported across figures. Minor gap: some supplementary figures are referenced but inaccessible in this version; human cohort clinical details are in Supplementary Table 1 without full description in the main text.

novelty_literature.justification: This study identifies a novel STING-TOX-HO-1 regulatory axis governing ferroptosis specifically in CD8+ T cells within the TME, distinct from previously described roles of STING/TOX in apoptosis or exhaustion. The finding that STING acts as a positive regulator of TOX (creating a feedback loop to suppress HO-1) is mechanistically original. The identification of lactate as an upstream TME-derived trigger of this axis links metabolic reprogramming to T-cell ferroptosis in a new way. Engineering STING/TOX-deficient T cells for ACT combination therapy represents a novel preclinical strategy, building on but substantially extending prior work.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a logical progression from phenotypic observations to mechanistic dissection to therapeutic application and clinical validation. The mechanistic model (Fig. 4l, Fig. 7g) effectively summarizes the proposed pathway. Writing is clear throughout, though some passages in the discussion are dense and would benefit from streamlining. A few typographical issues (e.g., 'agonizts' repeated) detract slightly. Figure legends are thorough and provide sufficient experimental detail.

key_strengths: Identifies a mechanistically novel STING-TOX-HO-1 axis governing CD8+ T cell ferroptosis in the TME, with multi-level validation across mouse and human systems
Comprehensive methodological toolkit: conditional KO mice, ACT models in multiple tumor lines, bulk and scRNA-seq, IHC cohort of 123 clinical specimens
Bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq raw data deposited in public repositories, supporting reproducibility
Lactate identified as a biologically plausible TME-derived trigger of the ferroptosis axis, linking Warburg metabolism to immune evasion
Preclinical therapeutic proof-of-concept for STING/TOX-deficient engineered T cells combined with ICB and chemotherapy is directly actionable
key_concerns: Clinical human validation is limited: scRNA-seq from only 2 cervical cancer patients and IHC cohort without prospective collection; limits direct translational claims
The paradoxical role of HO-1 (ferroptosis suppressor in this context vs. promoter in other contexts) is acknowledged but mechanistic clarity could be strengthened
In vivo mouse group sizes (3-4 mice/group) are at the lower boundary for rigorous in vivo tumor biology work
Repeated typographical errors ('agonizts') suggest incomplete manuscript proofreading
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a high-quality mechanistic oncology paper identifying a novel immune evasion mechanism (STING-TOX-HO-1 axis driving T-cell ferroptosis) with multi-system validation and translational relevance. The human clinical association data with 123 cervical cancer specimens provides meaningful preliminary translation. Tier 2 journals (Cancer Research, Nature Communications, CCR) would be appropriate given the mechanistic novelty and breadth of evidence; minor revisions to strengthen clinical translation section and correct typographical errors are warranted.
